end.parentNote: Saanvi used examples such as 6 + 10 = 16 and 10 + 15 = 25 to show that consecutive triangular numbers can add to a square number. They listed consecutive odd-number sums from 1 through 49 and identified the square results. One mix-up remained: 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 was said to equal 25, but it equals 24; this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask them to make a short table of odd-number sums, checking each total before naming its square root.
